get.summary: Get async video job status
get.description: Status of a video job the public API submitted. If `status` is `queued` or `processing`, call this same endpoint again after a short delay — there is no push notification, polling is the only way to learn when a job finishes. Terminal jobs (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`) are answered entirely from the local record and never need re-polling.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: Job ID returned by POST .../ai/videos/generate or POST .../ai/videos/tools/{tool_key}

message.example: Job status retrieved successfully. Poll this endpoint again if status is `queued` or `processing` — `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled` are terminal.

status.description: `queued`/`processing`: not finished — poll this same endpoint again after a short delay, result and credits are not yet available. `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`: terminal — no further polling needed, read `result` (if completed) and `credits` now.

stage.description: Raw upstream stage — informational, subject to change

result.description: Populated only when status is completed — contains the final video url, duration, resolution, and media_id. Null for every other status; do not treat a null result as a failure.

credits.description: Actual credits charged — null until terminal

error_code.description: Stable machine-readable failure reason, populated only when status is failed and the upstream engine supplied one (e.g. `file_download_error`)

error_message.description: Clean, human-readable failure reason, populated only when status is failed

error_details.description: Structured diagnostic detail for the failure, populated only when status is failed

get.summary: Bluesky summary KPIs — current vs previous period
get.description: Authored-post totals for the period plus the current profile counters. Note the absent metrics: there is no impressions, reach or click figure because the AT Protocol publishes none. `engagement_rate` is normalised by follower count, NOT impressions, so it is not comparable to the Facebook or LinkedIn engagement rate. `bookmarks` is null when no post in the period reported a bookmark count — that is 'unknown', not zero.

summary.description: Metrics broken into `current`, `previous`, absolute `difference` and `percentage` change.

capabilities.description: Which sections this platform can answer, and the reason for each unavailable metric.

get.summary: Bluesky follower trend, tracked since connection
get.description: Daily follower totals assembled from the snapshots ContentStudio retained. Bluesky exposes no historical follower data, so days before the first sync carry `tracked: false` and hold no value — they must be rendered as 'not tracked', never as zero followers. `capabilities.tracking.tracked_since` gives the first day with data.

tracked.description: False for days before the first retained snapshot.

get.summary: Bluesky engagement trend by post publish date
get.description: Engagement earned by the posts PUBLISHED on each day, measured at the last sync — not engagement that occurred on that day. Bluesky post counters are cumulative lifetime values and the protocol offers no per-interval metric, so a true daily interaction curve is not derivable. Accepts an optional comma-separated `media_type` filter (text, image, gallery, video, link, record, other).

get.summary: Bluesky publishing behaviour with a per-media-type rollup
get.description: Posting volume and engagement over time, plus a rollup broken down by media type (text, image, gallery, video, link, record, other) with a `total` row. Reposts by the account are excluded throughout — only authored posts are counted.

parameters.name: media_type
parameters.description: Comma-separated media types to include in the time series.

get.summary: Bluesky top authored posts (default 3)
get.description: Highest-performing authored posts. `order_by` accepts engagement, engagement_rate, likes, reposts, replies, quotes, bookmarks or published_at — there is deliberately no reach or impressions option, because no such measurement exists; an unrecognised value falls back to engagement rather than fabricating an order. `bookmark_count` may be null, meaning the value was not reported.

last_synced_at.description: When these cumulative counters were read.

get.summary: Bluesky paginated post table (default 15)
get.description: Same payload and sort options as top-posts with a larger default page size, for the sortable posts table.

get.summary: Bluesky single post detail
get.description: One authored post by its record key (rkey — the last segment of the at:// uri). The lookup is by identity and the date window never filters the result, so a post older than the dashboard range is still retrievable. The window is REQUIRED nonetheless — upstream validates it before it reads `post_id` — so it must be sent rather than omitted.

200.description: Post retrieved successfully. `post` is null when no such post is stored for this account.

get.summary: Bluesky posting cadence by weekday
get.description: How many posts were published on each weekday. The weekday is computed from the publish time in the requested timezone, so a workspace outside UTC sees its own days.

get.summary: Bluesky top hashtags by engagement
get.description: Top hashtags from richtext tag facets and the record's explicit tags. Tags are stored and returned lowercase so one tag aggregates into one row instead of splitting across casings. Bluesky publishes no hashtag reach or search-volume metric, so these are usage and engagement figures only.

get.summary: Which Bluesky metrics are available, and why the rest are not
get.description: Machine-readable statement of what this platform can answer. Consumers should read `unavailable` rather than hardcoding the gaps, and must render those metrics as unavailable — not as zero. `tracking.tracked_since` is the first day a follower snapshot was retained; nothing before it exists or can be backfilled.

post.summary: Top 5 posts per network for the selected campaigns & labels
post.description: Same payload and response as the posts endpoint, except `limit` is ignored: this always returns 5 posts per selected network, merged and globally ordered by `sort_by`. Unlike the posts endpoint, `impressions` and `reach` are filled on networks that do not report them (TikTok ← view count; YouTube reach ← views; Pinterest reach ← impressions) so `engagement`, `impressions` and `reach` are rankable everywhere and no network comes back empty for lack of the metric. The substituted value is what the response returns, so the two endpoints can legitimately report different `impressions`/`reach` for the same post despite the identical envelope. get.summary: Threads summary KPIs — current vs previous period
get.description: Post totals for the period alongside the account-level totals for the same days. The two sets are DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS and will not match: `likes`/`replies`/`reposts`/`quotes` count interactions on posts PUBLISHED in the window, while `account_likes`/`account_replies`/`account_reposts`/`account_quotes` count interactions that happened in the window across every post the account has ever made. There is no impressions or reach figure because Threads publishes none; `profile_views` is profile views, not post impressions. `engagement_rate` is normalised by follower count, NOT impressions, so it is not comparable to the Facebook or LinkedIn engagement rate. `views` and `shares` are null when no post in the period reported them — Meta labels both post metrics 'in development' — and are excluded from every engagement total for that reason.

get.summary: Threads follower trend, tracked since connection
get.description: Daily follower totals assembled from the snapshots ContentStudio retained. Meta's `followers_count` is point-in-time and ignores any date range, so there is no follower history before the first sync and none can be obtained later. Read `tracked` on every point: `tracked: true` is a measurement; `tracked: false` with a non-zero `followers_count` is a value legitimately carried forward from an earlier day; `tracked: false` with `followers_count: 0` is a day BEFORE tracking began and must be rendered as a gap, never as zero followers. `profile_views` is never carried forward — an untracked day has no measured views. The roll-up reports `followers_start` and `followers_end` as the first and last OBSERVED values, so `net_growth` goes negative for an account that lost followers.

tracked.description: False for days with no retained snapshot. Combined with followers_count it distinguishes a measurement, a carried-forward value and an untracked gap.

get.summary: Threads account activity — the true per-day series
get.description: What happened on each day ACROSS THE WHOLE ACCOUNT: profile views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes and link clicks. This is the only genuinely per-day engagement measurement Threads offers, and it is deliberately separate from `engagement`, which buckets lifetime post counters by publish date. The two answer different questions and must not be plotted on one axis. Nothing here is carried forward — these are event counts, not levels — so read `tracked` to tell a day with no snapshot from a genuinely quiet one.

tracked.description: False for days with no retained snapshot. An untracked day reads as zero and must be rendered as a gap.

get.summary: Threads engagement trend by post publish date
get.description: Engagement earned by the posts PUBLISHED on each day, measured at the last sync — not engagement that occurred on that day. Threads post counters are cumulative lifetime values, so a true daily interaction curve is not derivable from them; use `activity` for that. Accepts an optional comma-separated `media_type` filter using Meta's own vocabulary (TEXT_POST, IMAGE, VIDEO, CAROUSEL_ALBUM, AUDIO, REPOST_FACADE); values are matched case-insensitively.

get.summary: Threads publishing behaviour and per-media-type breakdown
get.description: The same daily series as `engagement`, plus a roll-up per media type and a `total` row. Media types use Meta's own vocabulary and are stored verbatim, so a type Meta adds later appears as itself rather than as 'other'. REPOST_FACADE rows are reposts of other accounts' posts: Meta returns no insights for them at all, so they carry no engagement — that is 'not measured', not 'performed badly'. The total's engagement rate is post-weighted, not the mean of the per-type rates.

get.summary: Threads top posts for the period
get.description: Posts ranked by the requested metric, defaulting to total engagement. `insights_available: false` means Meta returned no insights for that post — always the case for a repost of another account's post — so its zeroes are 'not measured' rather than 'nobody engaged'. `view_count` and `reshare_count` are null when Meta did not report them; render a dash, not a 0. `media_url` and `thumbnail` are signed, EXPIRING CDN urls and must be re-read rather than cached indefinitely. label.description: Localised display name, matching the wording used in the product.

used.description: Bytes for `media_storage`, a count for everything else — `note` says which.

limit.description: Null when the entitlement is unlimited, in which case `note` says so.

remaining.description: Null whenever `limit` is. Never negative: usage can exceed a limit after a downgrade, in which case this is 0.

scope.description: What `used` counts. `workspace` is this workspace alone; `account` is every workspace the account owner has. Account-wide: workspaces, social_accounts, team_members, listening_topics, automations, media_storage. The credit counters are per-workspace.

is_on_plan.description: False when the plan does not carry this at all — distinct from a fully consumed allowance, which `limit: null` alone cannot express.

NOTE: this field is an OBJECT only when overrides exist; a post with no overrides (i.e. the composer used one shared box) returns an EMPTY ARRAY `[]`, not `{}`. Decode it as a loose/optional map, and treat `[]` as `no overrides`. Only the platforms that actually carry their own copy appear.
